people.paul.role: Prisoner who writes to Philemon about Onesimus
people.paul.meaning: Paul writes from chains and calls himself aged. He chooses to appeal and not to command. He asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul. He offers to repay anything Onesimus owes, and he signs this with his own hand.
people.timothy.role: Brother named with Paul in the greeting
people.timothy.meaning: Paul names Timothy as a brother in the first line. Timothy sends the greeting with Paul. The letter says nothing else about him.
people.jesus.role: Lord named in the greetings, the thanks, and the blessing
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus. He ends with grace from the Lord Jesus Christ.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul gives thanks for Philemon’s faith toward the Lord Jesus. He asks that Onesimus be a beloved brother in the Lord. The letter ends with the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ.
people.philemon.role: Beloved fellow worker asked to receive Onesimus
people.philemon.meaning: Paul thanks Philemon for his love and for refreshing the saints. Then Paul asks him to receive Onesimus as a beloved brother. Paul wants Philemon to act by free will. Paul also asks him to prepare a guest room.
people.onesimus.role: Paul’s child, sent back to Philemon
people.onesimus.meaning: Paul became his father in chains. Paul calls him once useless and now useful. Paul sends him back to Philemon and asks Philemon to receive him as a brother. The letter does not say how Philemon answered.
people.epaphras.meaning: Paul calls Epaphras his fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. Epaphras sends greetings to Philemon. The letter says nothing else about him.
sources.web.summary: The full Scripture text is the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: Paul is the named writer. The guide did not check authorship, dates, Greek forms, or manuscripts. It did not check why Onesimus was away, where Paul was, or Onesimus’s legal freedom. It did not check what Philemon did later. It does not name Colossae or a prison city.
sources.pietz-philemon.summary: Pietz stresses changed relationships. She says it is unclear whether Paul asks for legal freedom.
sources.pietz-philemon.limits: This is Pietz’s own reading. The guide did not check her runaway theory or the legal setting. It did not check the history of slavery or the outcome. The letter does not record Onesimus’s own response.
